original_question: Characterize exactly which maps or permutations f : L -> L over a finite field L have the spectrum-invariance property that, for every nonzero scalar b in L, the Fourier spectrum of f is the same as the Fourier spectrum of the scalar multiple bf.
target_in_paper: Section 2, the unnumbered open problem on invariance of the Fourier distribution: determine the maps f for which spec(f_b)=spec(f) for every b∈L×, after observing that power permutations have this property.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly isolates the paper’s actual classification problem: over a finite field, identify those maps f whose Fourier spectrum is unchanged when the output is multiplied by any nonzero scalar b. It also correctly keeps the focus on the power-permutation phenomenon that motivates the question.
missing_details: The paper formulates this for maps f:L→L, not only for permutations; power permutations are the motivating example, not the full scope of the problem.
The ambient field should be fixed as a finite field L=F_q of characteristic p.
The Fourier transform must be defined using the canonical additive character μ(x)=exp(2πi Tr_{L/F_p}(x)/p).

The relevant transformed family is f_b(x)=b f(x), and the Fourier coefficients are defined with the paper’s convention ^hat{f_b}(a)=Σ_{x∈L} μ(bf(x)-ax) (equivalently, with the paper’s notation for the Fourier coefficient at a).
The paper’s 'spectrum' here is the Fourier distribution/multiset of values as a ranges over L, not merely the underlying set of distinct values.
The quantifier is over every nonzero scalar b∈L×.
The motivating identity for power permutations should be made explicit: if f(x)=x^s with gcd(s,q-1)=1, then ^hat{f_b}(a)=^hat{f}(a b^{-1/s}), hence the spectra coincide.
This is posed as an open problem; the paper does not give a classification theorem here.
If one wants the question to be fully stand-alone, one should specify that equality of spectra means equality of the multisets { ^hat{f_b}(a) : a∈L } and { ^hat{f}(a) : a∈L }.
Your draft does not need extra degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or 'sufficiently large m' conditions, because those belong to other papers/problems, not to this one.
refined_question: Let L=F_q be a finite field of characteristic p, let μ(x)=exp(2πi Tr_{L/F_p}(x)/p) be its canonical additive character, and for a map f:L→L and b∈L define f_b(x)=b f(x) and Fourier coefficients by ^hat{f_b}(a)=Σ_{x∈L} μ(bf(x)-ax) for a∈L. If spec(f_b) denotes the Fourier spectrum/distribution of f_b, i.e. the multiset { ^hat{f_b}(a) : a∈L }, then every power permutation f(x)=x^s with gcd(s,q-1)=1 satisfies spec(f_b)=spec(f_1) for all b∈L×. Determine all maps f:L→L for which spec(f_b)=spec(f_1) for every b∈L×.
justification: The draft is closest not to Conjecture 1.1 itself, but to the later unnumbered problem in the section on invariance of the Fourier distribution. The paper first notes that power permutations x↦x^s satisfy spec(f_b)=spec(f) because the Fourier coefficients are permuted as a varies, and then asks exactly which maps have this property. I therefore kept the question narrowly on classifying such maps, while restoring the paper’s hidden notation: the canonical additive character, the definition of f_b, the Fourier coefficient convention, and the fact that 'spectrum' means Fourier distribution/multiset. I did not broaden the problem to vanishing conjectures, rationality of spectra, or three-/four-valued spectrum questions, since those are neighboring topics in the introduction and later sections rather than the exact open problem your draft targets.
